contracts.signal: Cerebras' 10-Q: under the December 2025 Master Relationship Agreement (MRA), OpenAI committed to purchase 750MW of AI inference compute capacity and related services, with deployment expected in tranches during 2026 through 2028, over a term of three or four years extendable by OpenAI to a maximum of five years; OpenAI also has the option to purchase an additional 1.25GW of capacity for deployment in tranches by the end of 2030, for up to a total of 2.0GW. Cerebras must deliver capacity tranches across specified numbers of data centers with minimum capacity thresholds; the MRA contains exclusivity provisions restricting work with certain named competitors of OpenAI. Revenue recognized under the arrangement was $56.8 million in Q2 2026 and $74.4 million in the six months ended June 30, 2026, and a significant amount of the $25.4 billion RPO is attributable to the MRA.

contracts.signal: Cerebras' 10-Q: in June 2026 Cerebras entered into a global hardware leasing agreement (the AWS Commercial Agreement) to deploy a joint compute solution in AWS data centers, together with related software and support services. It includes an initial multi-year lease of Cerebras systems, options for future procurement of products and services, pricing commitments, exclusivity, and minimum manufacturing capacity guarantees in favor of AWS. As of June 30, 2026 the lease commencement conditions had not been satisfied, so no revenue had been recognized under the arrangement.

contracts.signal: Cerebras' 10-Q: Cerebras depends on one third-party foundry, TSMC, to manufacture its proprietary processor and TSMC fabricates all of its wafers; the WSE-2 was manufactured on TSMC's 7nm process and the WSE-3 on TSMC's 5nm process. Cerebras has no formalized long-term supply or allocation commitments from TSMC, the wafer is a long-lead-time component, and the company has experienced delays in securing tape-out slots.
